q: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and _____.
e: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and biosphere. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms are called a _____ cycle.
e: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms are called a biogeochemical cycle. A biogeochemical cycle moves an element through rocks, water, air, and living things.

q: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and _____.
e: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and sediments. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The processes involved in the carbon cycle include photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and _____.
e: The processes involved in the carbon cycle include photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and combustion. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: The extra carbon dioxide absorbed by the ocean is lowering its pH through a process called _____.
e: The extra carbon dioxide absorbed by the ocean is lowering its pH through a process called ocean acidification. Eutrophication: cations form when atoms lose electrons. Biomagnification: cations form when atoms lose electrons.

q: The nitrogen cycle involves nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and _____.
e: The nitrogen cycle involves nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and denitrification. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Unlike many other cycling elements, _____ cannot be found in the air and mainly cycles through water, soil and sediments.
e: Unlike many other cycling elements, phosphorus cannot be found in the air and mainly cycles through water, soil and sediments. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions $PO_4^{3-}$ and _____.
e: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions PO43- and HPO42-. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land through their _____, which contains a high level of phosphorus.
e: Marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land through their guano, which contains a high level of phosphorus. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Sulphur is one of the components that make up _____ and vitamins.
e: Sulphur is one of the components that make up proteins and vitamins. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water in the atmosphere to produce _____ acid.
e: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water in the atmosphere to produce sulphuric acid. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus from fertiliser runoff cause excessive growth of _____ in water bodies.
e: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus from fertiliser runoff cause excessive growth of algae in water bodies. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The death and decay of aquatic plants deplete dissolved oxygen, leading to the creation of _____ zones in lakes and rivers.
e: The death and decay of aquatic plants deplete dissolved oxygen, leading to the creation of dead zones in lakes and rivers. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The extraction of metals like copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases _____ dioxide.
e: The extraction of metals like copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases sulphur dioxide. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The 7 R's of a green environment include Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and _____.
e: The 7 R's of a green environment include Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and Recycle. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: _____ chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances.
e: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and _____ take a variety of chemical forms.
e: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur take a variety of chemical forms. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and _____.
e: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and skeletons. Ocean acidification is the long-term drop in seawater pH as the ocean takes up extra CO2.

q: Sulphur dioxide can react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals to produce _____ salts.
e: Sulphur dioxide can react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals to produce sulphur salts. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: A green environment supports practices like informed consumption, conservation practices and investment in _____ energy.
e: A green environment supports practices like informed consumption, conservation practices and investment in renewable energy. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living _____.
e: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living organisms. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: In the fossilisation process, animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and _____.
e: In the fossilisation process, animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and minerals. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Phosphorus is a building block of certain parts of the human body including _____ and animal bones.
e: Phosphorus is a building block of certain parts of the human body including DNA and animal bones. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Phosphate salts released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by _____.
e: Phosphate salts released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by plants. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Sulphur can enter the atmosphere through natural sources like volcanic eruptions, bacterial processes, or decaying _____.
e: Sulphur can enter the atmosphere through natural sources like volcanic eruptions, bacterial processes, or decaying organisms. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low _____.
e: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low concentrations. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature but can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic _____.
e: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature but can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic anhydride. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and _____ oxidation states in nature.
e: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and +5 oxidation states in nature. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks are the main sources of _____ contamination.
e: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks are the main sources of groundwater contamination. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Compounds like calcium arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and _____.
e: Compounds like calcium arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and semiconductors. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium _____.
e: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium oxide. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Tobacco smoking is a significant source of _____ exposure.
e: Tobacco smoking is a significant source of cadmium exposure. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, and _____ materials.
e: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, and photovoltaic materials. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: In the environment, lead primarily exists in the +2 and _____ oxidation states.
e: In the environment, lead primarily exists in the +2 and +4 oxidation states. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal _____ engines.
e: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion engines. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of _____, and in the production of paint and alloys.
e: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of batteries, and in the production of paint and alloys. An alloy is a mixture of metals with useful combined properties.

q: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into _____ by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and fungi.
e: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into methylmercury by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and fungi. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Methylmercury bioaccumulates in fish and _____.
e: Methylmercury bioaccumulates in fish and shellfish. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, and _____.
e: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, and eyes. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Pesticides are often grouped into families such as organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates, and _____.
e: Pesticides are often grouped into families such as organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates, and pyrethroids. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The transfer of pesticides includes processes like volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, and _____.
e: The transfer of pesticides includes processes like volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, and absorption. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown by microbes, chemical reactions, and _____.
e: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown by microbes, chemical reactions, and photodegradation. Photodegradation is breakdown caused by sunlight.

q: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are carbon-based organic compounds that are long-lasting and resist _____.
e: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are carbon-based organic compounds that are long-lasting and resist breakdown. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: POPs are chemically stable and lipophilic, meaning they accumulate in the _____ tissue of living organisms.
e: POPs are chemically stable and lipophilic, meaning they accumulate in the fatty tissue of living organisms. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: VOCs react with nitrogen oxides under sunlight to form _____, which helps form fine particulates.
e: VOCs react with nitrogen oxides under sunlight to form ozone, which helps form fine particulates. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in _____ that reduces visibility.
e: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in smog that reduces visibility. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and _____ into the atmosphere.
e: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and polychlorinated biphenyls into the atmosphere. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Arsenic compounds cause acute and chronic effects depending on species and time of _____.
e: Arsenic compounds cause acute and chronic effects depending on species and time of exposure. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Cadmium exists as the _____ oxidation state in nature.
e: Cadmium exists as the +2 oxidation state in nature. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and neurological effects in _____.
e: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and neurological effects in vertebrates. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged _____ particles.
e: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged clay particles. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Pesticides can cause short-term adverse health effects, called acute effects, as well as _____ adverse effects that occur months or years later.
e: Pesticides can cause short-term adverse health effects, called acute effects, as well as chronic adverse effects that occur months or years later. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like DDT are examples of _____.
e: Industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like DDT are examples of POPs. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: VOCs are generally man-made carbon-based molecules such as paint thinners, dry cleaning fluid, and nail polish _____.
e: VOCs are generally man-made carbon-based molecules such as paint thinners, dry cleaning fluid, and nail polish bottle. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form _____.
e: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form ozone. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay of heavy nuclei generating alpha particles, beta particles and _____ rays.
e: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay of heavy nuclei generating alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays. Radioactivity is when an unstable nucleus throws out alpha, beta, or gamma radiation to lose energy.

q: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of _____.
e: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of paper. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by _____ foil.
e: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by aluminium foil. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, _____, or other heavy shielding.
e: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, lead, or other heavy shielding. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from _____ elements.
e: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from inert elements. Background radiation is the ionising radiation that is already around you from rocks, air, and space.

q: Cosmic radiation from _____ also contributes to the background radiation around us.
e: Cosmic radiation from space also contributes to the background radiation around us. The core: core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the human body, mainly naturally occurring _____.
e: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the human body, mainly naturally occurring potassium-40. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The radioactive gas, _____, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and underground water sources.
e: The radioactive gas, argon, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and underground water sources. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause _____ cancer.
e: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause lung cancer. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are _____ materials produced from a breeder reactor.
e: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are fissile materials produced from a breeder reactor. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Ionisation smoke detectors use _____ as a source of alpha particles.
e: Ionisation smoke detectors use americium-241 as a source of alpha particles. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and _____ objects.
e: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and organic objects. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear _____ systems.
e: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear propulsion systems. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating _____.
e: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating cancer. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Nuclear reactors generate electricity by using fissile heavy atoms instead of _____ fuels.
e: Nuclear reactors generate electricity by using fissile heavy atoms instead of fossil fuels. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and _____.
e: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and radiation. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radionuclides found in water include potassium-40, radium-226 and _____.
e: Radionuclides found in water include potassium-40, radium-226 and oxygen-16. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital _____.
e: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital organs. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radioactive pollution is the result of released _____ in the environment.
e: Radioactive pollution is the result of released radionuclides in the environment. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive _____.
e: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive energy. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Organic farming uses fertilisers of organic origin such as compost manure, green manure, and _____ instead of chemical fertilisers.
e: Organic farming uses fertilisers of organic origin such as compost manure, green manure, and bone meal instead of chemical fertilisers. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The neem leaves consist of insecticidal ingredients and can be used as an _____.
e: The neem leaves consist of insecticidal ingredients and can be used as an insecticide. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Plant-based insecticidal soaps leave no nasty residue, are non-toxic to animals, and do not harm _____ insects.
e: Plant-based insecticidal soaps leave no nasty residue, are non-toxic to animals, and do not harm beneficial insects. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The municipal and non-hazardous industrial wastes are converted to energy by direct burning in a process known as waste gasification or _____.
e: The municipal and non-hazardous industrial wastes are converted to energy by direct burning in a process known as waste gasification or pyrolysis. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In waste gasification, organic content wastes produce a mixture of hydrogen and carbon _____.
e: In waste gasification, organic content wastes produce a mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Bioethanol is produced by converting the sugar content of any starchy material into alcohol with the evolution of carbon _____.
e: Bioethanol is produced by converting the sugar content of any starchy material into alcohol with the evolution of carbon dioxide. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Biodiesel oil is synthesised from plant oils by removing the by-product _____ molecule, which is valuable for soap production.
e: Biodiesel oil is synthesised from plant oils by removing the by-product glycerine molecule, which is valuable for soap production. Biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: The main purpose of wastewater treatment is to remove suspended solids, organic carbon, nutrients, inorganic salts, heavy metals and _____.
e: The main purpose of wastewater treatment is to remove suspended solids, organic carbon, nutrients, inorganic salts, heavy metals and pathogens. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Photocatalysts like binary metal oxides nanomaterials (e.g., $TiO_2$, $ZnO$, $Fe_2O_3$) are used to mineralise, decompose, and _____ pollutants.
e: Photocatalysts like binary metal oxides nanomaterials (e.g., TiO2, ZnO, Fe2O3) are used to mineralise, decompose, and oxidise pollutants.

q: Previously, tetraethyllead (TEL) was used as an anti-knocking agent, but nowadays it is replaced by methyl _____ ether (MTBE).
e: Previously, tetraethyllead (TEL) was used as an anti-knocking agent, but nowadays it is replaced by methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE). Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Bioplastics are derived from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch, vegetable oils and _____.
e: Bioplastics are derived from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch, vegetable oils and fats. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the liquid $CO_2$ cleaning process, liquid carbon dioxide replaces _____ which pollutes groundwater.
e: In the liquid CO2 cleaning process, liquid carbon dioxide replaces tetrachloroethene which pollutes groundwater. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Large amounts of adipic acid are used each year for the production of nylon, polyurethanes, lubricants and _____.
e: Large amounts of adipic acid are used each year for the production of nylon, polyurethanes, lubricants and plasticisers. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Chemists developed a green synthesis of adipic acid using _____, which is converted by an enzyme in genetically modified bacteria.
e: Chemists developed a green synthesis of adipic acid using glucose, which is converted by an enzyme in genetically modified bacteria. Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed specific biochemical reactions.

q: Hexavalent chromium plating produces hazardous waste including lead chromates and barium _____.
e: Hexavalent chromium plating produces hazardous waste including lead chromates and barium sulphate. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Trivalent chromium plating uses chromium sulphate or chromium _____ as its main ingredient.
e: Trivalent chromium plating uses chromium sulphate or chromium chloride as its main ingredient. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Vermilion is a red pigment originally made by grinding a powder of cinnabar, which is mercury(II) _____.
e: Vermilion is a red pigment originally made by grinding a powder of cinnabar, which is mercury(II) sulphide. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Arsenic trisulphide ($As_2S_3$) is used as _____ in works of art because of its bright yellow colour.
e: Arsenic trisulphide (As2S3) is used as orpiment in works of art because of its bright yellow colour. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Clove oil contains eugenol, while mint oil contains menthol and _____.
e: Clove oil contains eugenol, while mint oil contains menthol and pulegone. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Cinnamon oil contains _____ as its major organic compound.
e: Cinnamon oil contains cinnamaldehyde as its major organic compound. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Solar, wind, hydroelectric, biomass, biorefineries, geothermal, and _____ energy are important renewable resources.
e: Solar, wind, hydroelectric, biomass, biorefineries, geothermal, and tidal energy are important renewable resources. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The combustion of fossil fuel generates sulphur compounds whereas _____ does not.
e: The combustion of fossil fuel generates sulphur compounds whereas biodiesel does not. Biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: Green materials such as agricultural waste adsorbent, activated carbon, and rice husk-derived _____ materials are applied in wastewater treatment.
e: Green materials such as agricultural waste adsorbent, activated carbon, and rice husk-derived ceramic materials are applied in wastewater treatment. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Lemongrass oil contains citronellal and _____ as major components.
e: Lemongrass oil contains citronellal and geranial as major components. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Rosemary oil contains 1,8-cineole, and oil of oregano contains _____.
e: Rosemary oil contains 1,8-cineole, and oil of oregano contains carvacrol. Cinnamaldehyde: an aldehyde has a carbonyl attached to hydrogen.
